articles.title: EEUU tiene los modelos más caros y capaces del mundo. El problema es que China los tiene casi igual de buenos y mucho más baratos
articles.text:
Hace pocas semanas se lanzó DeepSeek V4-Flash, y esta semana hemos visto cómo han llegado dos espectaculares modelos más: Qwen3.8-Flash y GLM-5.3-Flash. Todos ellos destacan por ser buenos, bonitos y sobre todo, baratos. Antes los modelos de pesos abiertos chinos eran atractivos solo por su precio, pero ahora han logrado algo alucinante: ser casi tan buenos como los modelos frontera más avanzados de OpenAI y Anthropic. Cuidadín.
China aprieta. OpenAI, Anthropic y (a mayor distancia por ahora) Google siguen siendo normalmente los protagonistas a la hora de hablar de modelos frontera con el mayor rendimiento, pero las empresas chinas están comenzando a competir en otra métrica que puede acabar siendo igual de importante: cuánta inteligencia obtiene uno por cada dólar gastado. Los últimos lanzamientos de Alibaba, Z.ai y DeepSeek muestran una estrategia muy parecida: acercarse lo máximo posible a los mejores modelos occidentales mientras reducen el coste de utilizarlos hasta niveles casi imposibles de ignorar.
Qwen3.8-Flash, un ejemplo claro. Alibaba lo presenta como un adelanto de la futura arquitectura Qwen4: un modelo MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) de 125.000 millones de parámetros en el que solo unos 6.000 millones están activos en cada momento. La compañía afirma que compite con modelos mucho mayores en áreas de programación y tareas agénticas, pero lo hace con una API que cuesta apenas 0,16 /0,47 dólares por millón de tokens de de entrada / salida. Es un precio ridículo si lo comparamos con la competencia, y la eficiencia aquí es la que constituye el pilar de una arquitectura que amenaza la de los modelos de OpenAI y Anthropic.
Pero es que GLM-5.3-Flash es tan bueno o mejor. Lo conocimos estos días como Ox Alpha, el misterioso modelo del que todo el mundo hablaba y que resulta que era este nuevo modelo de Z.ai. Tiene 320.000 millones de parámetros, aunque activa solo 18.000 millones por token. Además tiene contexto de un millón de tokens y ya han publicado sus pesos abiertos con licencia MIT. Artificial Analysis le da 57 puntos en su Intelligence Index, muy cerca de los 60 de GLM-5.3 Max, pero su coste medio por tarea es de 0,09 dólares, frente a los 0,68 dóares de su hermano mayor. La diferencia de inteligencia es pequeña; la de precio, enorme.
La pregunta que cada vez es más importante. DeepSeek y modelos abiertos de empresas chinas en los últimos meses han planteado constantemente la misma pregunta: ¿cuánto podemos abaratar una IA antes de que deje de tener sentido pagar por otra? En DeepSeek V4-Flash los 0,22/0,66 dólares por millón de tokens de E/S (tras la subida de precios) ya eran una señal de alarma. Puede que no fuera el modelo más inteligen del mercado, pero sí era mucho más barato que GPT-5.6 Sol (4/20) o Claude Fable 5 (10/50).
Independencia occidcental. Las empresas chinas están descubriendo cómo diseñar sus modelos para que sean cada vez más eficientes y, por tanto, baratos. Técnicas como Mixture of Experts (para activar solo una pequeña parte de los parámetros totales), atención dispersa o lineal para evitar procesar innecesariamente todo el contexto, cachés más pequeñas y arquitecturas optimizadas para servir enormes cantidades de tokens demuestran cada vez más estar logrando hitos espectaculares.
Tokens a tutiplén. En el caso de GLM-5.3-Flash hay además otra señal llamativa: la infraestructura. Ox Alpha se ofreció gratuitamente con una capacidad anunciada de hasta 100 billones de tokens diarios, y Z.ai ha confirmado ahora que funcionaba íntegramente sobre chips chinos. SemiAnalysis añade que esa infraestructura logró una eficiencia de hardware y un coste por token comparables a los de GPU Nvidia. Los 100 billones de tokens cada día eran la capacidad anunciada, no el tráfico real, pero todo ello demuestra hasta qué punto China está empezando a construir no solo modelos competitivos, sino también la infraestructura doméstica necesaria para servirlos a gran escala.
La frontera de Pareto. En los últimos tiempos los responsables de Artificial Analysis destacan especialmente una gráfica a la que llaman "Índice de Inteligencia vs. Coste por tarea del Índice de Inteligencia". En el eje X está el coste por tarea. En el Y, lo "inteligente" que es el modelo. Ahí GLM-5.3-Flash rompe las métricas, y es el que mejor supera la denominada Frontera de Pareto. Un modelo resulta especialmente atractivo cuando no puedes conseguir mucha más capacidad sin pagar bastante más, y tanto GLM como Qwen logran desplazar esa frontera. No son los mejores, desde luego, pero ¿cuánto estás dispuesto a pagar para conseguir ese 5 o 10% más de "inteligencia"?
Modelos suficientemente buenos. Para usuarios y sobre todo empresas que necesitan resolver millones de consultas, programar tareas relativamente rutinarias o desplegar cientos de agentes no es necesario usar GPT-5.6 Sol o Claude Fable 5. Lo que necesitas es un modelo suficientemente bueno, fiable y barato. Ya hemos visto algo así otras veces en la industria tecnológica: el producto técnicamente mejor pude dominar la gama alta, pero el producto suficientemente bueno es el que logra hacerse con el volumen mayoritario gracias a su precio y disponibilidad.

articles.title: Manchester Airports Group says hackers stole travelers' data
articles.text:
The Manchester Airports Group (MAG) disclosed that hackers breached its systems and stole customer data, including Wi-Fi sign-ups from Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports.
The intruder did not access customer payment details, and the attack had no impact on airport operations, the company said.
A statement from the company today notes that the exfiltrated data also "relates to car park, lounge and Fast Track bookings." The list of compromised details includes customers' email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers, and postcodes.
“The incident has not resulted in any operational disruption,” assured the organization, adding that “Airport operations remain unaffected and customer parking services continue to operate normally.”
Out of an abundance of caution, MAG has temporarily suspended its online “Manage My Booking” service and is instead directing travelers to use its phone line.
MAG is the UK’s largest airport operator, and owner of Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports, which together handle over 66 million passengers yearly.
The company employs 40,000 people and generates annual revenue of £1.5 billion.
After discovering the intrusion, MAG says that it moved quickly to contain it, restricting access to the affected systems, engaging with external experts, and notifying law enforcement.
Potentially exposed customers are advised to remain alert for suspicious communications and avoid clicking on links arriving via email or SMS.
MAG stresses that it will never ask customers for payment card information, banking details, or passwords. Customers should reject and report to the authorities any attempts to obtain personal, financial, or other sensitive information.
People are also encouraged to follow NCSC’s post-breach recommendations to stay safe.
The company says it has contacted impacted customers directly, but did not disclose the number of affected individuals.
Local media reported that data of up to 8.9 million travelers may have been exposed, citing private MAG statements; however, BleepingComputer has not been able to confirm the figure.
At the time of writing, no ransomware or data extortion groups have claimed the attack publicly.

articles.title: Redmi Note 17 Pro Max: Release date, price and specs
articles.text:
Table of contents
Xiaomi launched the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max globally on August 27, 2026. It is the first Pro Max phone in the Redmi Note series, and it sits above the Redmi Note 17 Pro as the top model in the lineup.
The phone’s biggest selling point is its battery. Depending on where you buy it, you get a 9,210mAh or 10,000mAh battery, paired with 100W fast charging. Below, you’ll find the release date, price, full specs, and how the Pro Max compares to the standard Note 17 and Note 17 Pro.
Redmi Note 17 Pro Max at a glance
| Spec | Details | 
|---|---|
| Official name | Redmi Note 17 Pro Max 5G | 
| Global launch date | August 27, 2026 | 
| Display | 6.83-inch AMOLED, 1.5K resolution, up to 120Hz | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 | 
| Battery | 9,210mAh or 10,000mAh, depending on your market | 
| Rear cameras | 50MP main with OIS and 8MP ultrawide | 
| Front camera | 32MP | 
| Charging | 100W wired | 
| Starting price | About $499 (varies by market) | 
Redmi Note 17 Pro Max release date
Xiaomi announced the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max on August 27, 2026, as part of a global launch that also included the Redmi Note 17, Redmi Note 17 5G, and Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G. Sale dates and prices differ by country, so check the details for your market below.
| Market | Date and details | 
|---|---|
| Japan | Sales start August 28, 2026, through Xiaomi, Amazon Japan, electronics retailers, SoftBank, Y!mobile, and IIJmio. | 
| Singapore | Pre-orders run from August 27 to September 2. Sales open on September 3. | 
| Malaysia | The local launch event is set for September 2, 2026. Xiaomi has not shared local pricing yet. | 
| Europe | Retailers began listing the phone on August 27, with delivery from August 29 in some countries. | 
| Australia | Xiaomi has an Australian launch page for the 9,210mAh version. Confirm the exact sale date closer to the time. | 
| United States | Reports say Xiaomi is not planning an official US release for this phone. | 
| India | A tipster claims the Pro and Pro Max will launch on September 15, but Xiaomi India has not confirmed this. | 
Is it coming to Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, or Ghana?
Xiaomi has not confirmed a release date for the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max in Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, or Ghana. None of these countries has a local product page for the phone yet, and Xiaomi’s Nigeria site still shows the Redmi Note 15 series as its newest model.
Reports suggest the phone is headed to more African markets, but there’s no confirmed country-level pricing or sale date yet. If you see the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max for sale locally before an official announcement, treat it as an imported unit. It may not come with a local warranty.
Redmi Note 17 Pro Max price
Xiaomi has confirmed official prices in a few markets, while others are still pending. Here’s what we know so far.
| Market | Configuration | Price | 
|---|---|---|
| International (reported) | Entry model | About $499 | 
| Europe | 8GB/256GB | €599.90 | 
| Europe | 8GB/512GB | About €649 (confirm against Xiaomi’s official price before you buy) | 
| Japan | 8GB/256GB | ¥79,980 | 
| Japan | 8GB/512GB | ¥99,980 | 
| Singapore | 8GB/256GB | S$749 (S$669 launch price) | 
| Singapore | 8GB/512GB | S$849 (S$769 launch price) | 
| Malaysia | Pending | Expected at the September 2 launch | 
| India | Pending | No official price yet | 
What would it cost in Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Ghana?
Xiaomi hasn’t announced local pricing for these markets. As a rough guide, converting the European price range (€599.90 to €649) at rates checked on August 27, 2026 gives you:
- Nigeria: about ₦968,000 to ₦1.05 million
- Kenya: about KSh90,400 to KSh97,800
- South Africa: about R11,170 to R12,084
- Ghana: about GH₵7,829 to GH₵8,469
These are direct currency conversions and don’t include shipping, import duties, taxes, or retailer markup. Your actual price will likely be higher once the phone reaches local markets officially, and prices may shift with currency changes.
Redmi Note 17 Pro Max specs
1. Display and design
- A 6.83-inch AMOLED display with 1.5K resolution (2772 x 1280) and up to 120Hz refresh rate
- Peak brightness of up to 3,500 nits, with support for HDR10+ and Dolby Vision
- Gorilla Glass Victus 2 protection on the front
- Weighs 229.5g and comes in Black, Cloud Blush, and other colours depending on your region
Cloud Blush shifts from white to a pink-orange tone in sunlight or under UV light.
2. Chipset and performance
The Redmi Note 17 Pro Max runs on a Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chip, built on a 4nm process with a top CPU speed of 2.6GHz. Qualcomm says this chip delivers up to 21% better graphics performance and 20% faster app launches than the chip it replaces.
In everyday use, like browsing and watching videos, the phone runs smoothly according to early hands-on tests. Heavy gaming at high settings can cause some stuttering. The Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 sits in Qualcomm’s mid-range lineup, so the Pro Max name doesn’t mean flagship-level power.
3. Cameras
- A 50MP main camera with optical image stabilisation (OIS)
- An 8MP ultrawide camera
- A 32MP front camera for selfies and video calls
- Video recording up to 4K at 30fps on both the front and rear cameras
Compared to the Redmi Note 15 Pro+’s 200MP main camera, this is a step down in resolution. Higher megapixels don’t always mean better photos, but it’s worth knowing if you’re upgrading from that model.
4. Battery and charging
- A 10,000mAh battery in Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, and Xiaomi’s global markets, or a 9,210mAh battery in Europe and Australia
- 100W wired charging, with Xiaomi claiming a full charge in a little over an hour
- Up to 27W reverse wired charging, so you can charge other devices from your phone
- Xiaomi says the battery keeps at least 80% of its capacity after 1,600 charge cycles, or roughly six years of typical use
One independent test in Singapore recorded a charge from 0% to 50% in 34 minutes, and close to two hours for a full charge, so actual charging time may run longer than Xiaomi’s marketing figures suggest.
The charger isn’t included everywhere. Japan’s retail box includes a 100W adapter, but Xiaomi’s global page says the standard package doesn’t. Check your local listing before you buy.
5. Durability
- IP68 and IP69 water and dust resistance in most markets, with the full IP66/IP68/IP69/IP69K rating in global and Singapore units
- SGS-certified to survive a 3-meter drop onto hard granite in testing
- Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on the display
- TÜV SÜD certification covering battery, drop, and water resistance tests
Even with these ratings, water resistance can wear down over time, and Xiaomi’s warranty still has exclusions. Treat these ratings as durability advantages, not a guarantee.
6. Software
- Runs Xiaomi’s HyperOS 3 out of the box, on top of Android 16
- Six years of security updates confirmed in Japan and Singapore
- Xiaomi’s 72-month like-new claim refers to an internal ageing test, not a promise of six years of major Android upgrades
- AI features like Circle to Search, Google Gemini, AI Writing, AI Interpreter, and AI Erase Pro, though availability depends on your region and language
7. Connectivity and other features
- 5G and 4G support, with dual SIM options that vary by market, and eSIM support in some regions
- Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 6.0
- NFC and an infrared blaster, both dependent on your region
- An in-display fingerprint sensor, face unlock, and USB-C charging, but no 3.5mm headphone jack or microSD card slot
Why does the battery size change by market?
You’ll see both 9,210mAh and 10,000mAh listed for the same phone, and both numbers are correct. Xiaomi sells different battery configurations depending on where you buy the phone. Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, and Xiaomi’s global materials list a 10,000mAh battery. Europe and Australia get a 9,210mAh version instead, which reportedly uses a dual-cell design rather than a single cell. Xiaomi hasn’t explained why the capacities differ, so don’t assume it’s due to regional regulations until the company confirms it.
Redmi Note 17 vs Redmi Note 17 Pro vs Redmi Note 17 Pro Max
Here’s how the three Note 17 models compare, based on Singapore’s launch lineup, where all three were announced together with official prices.
| Spec | Note 17 | Note 17 Pro | Note 17 Pro Max | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Display | 6.99-inch AMOLED, 120Hz | 6.83-inch 1.5K AMOLED, 120Hz | 6.83-inch 1.5K AMOLED, 120Hz | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 | Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 | Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 | 
| Battery | 7,700mAh | 8,340mAh | 10,000mAh (Singapore) | 
| Charging | 45W | 67W | 100W plus 27W reverse charging | 
| Main camera | 50MP | 50MP OIS plus 8MP ultrawide | 50MP OIS plus 8MP ultrawide | 
| IP rating | IP65 | Up to IP69K | Up to IP69K | 
| Starting price (Singapore) | S$449 | S$549 | S$749 | 
The standard Note 17 focuses on value, the Pro adds a sharper display and stronger water resistance, and the Pro Max pushes battery size and charging speed further than either one.
How it compares to the Redmi Note 15 Pro+
| Spec | Note 15 Pro+ | Note 17 Pro Max | 
|---|---|---|
| Main camera | 200MP OIS | 50MP OIS | 
| Battery | 6,500mAh | 9,210mAh or 10,000mAh | 
| Charging | 100W wired, up to 22.5W reverse | 100W wired, up to 27W reverse | 
| Weight | About 207g to 208g | 229.5g | 
| Software at launch | HyperOS 2 | HyperOS 3 | 
The Pro Max gives you a much bigger battery, faster storage, and newer software than the Note 15 Pro+. The older phone still wins on camera resolution, with its 200MP main sensor beating the Pro Max’s 50MP setup, and it’s noticeably lighter too. Don’t expect the Pro Max to improve on every spec, since the camera is one area where it falls behind.
Where to buy the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max
- Japan: Xiaomi’s website and stores, Amazon Japan, Rakuten, Yahoo Shopping, electronics retailers, and through SoftBank, Y!mobile, or IIJmio
- Singapore: Xiaomi’s website, Xiaomi Stores, Shopee, and Lazada
- Europe: Amazon and major electronics retailers in Spain and Germany already list the phone
- Malaysia: Official channels and pricing will be confirmed at the September 2 launch
Buying in Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, or Ghana
Until Xiaomi publishes an official local page, treat any listing you find as an import. Before you buy, check these points:
- Confirm whether the unit has the 9,210mAh or 10,000mAh battery
- Check that it supports your local 4G and 5G bands, and whether the charger and correct plug type are included
- Ask the seller whether Xiaomi’s local service centres will honour the warranty
- Confirm that eSIM and NFC work with your network, if you plan to use them
Frequently asked questions
Q) When was the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max released?
A) Xiaomi announced the phone globally on August 27, 2026. Japan started sales on August 28, and Singapore opens general sales on September 3. Other markets have their own dates, listed above.
Q) How much does the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max cost?
A) The international starting price is reported at about $499. In Europe, the 8GB/256GB version costs €599.90. Japan’s price starts at ¥79,980, and Singapore’s starts at S$749.
Q) Does the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max support 5G?
A) Yes. The phone’s full name includes 5G, and its spec sheet lists broad 5G band support across markets.
Q) Does it have a 9,210mAh or 10,000mAh battery?
A) Both exist. Europe and Australia get the 9,210mAh version. Japan, Singapore, and Malaysia get the 10,000mAh version.
Q) What cameras does the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max have?
A) It has a 50MP main camera with OIS and an 8MP ultrawide camera on the back, plus a 32MP front camera.
Q) Is the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max coming to Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, or Ghana?
A) Xiaomi hasn’t confirmed a release date or price for any of these four markets yet. Imported units may show up before an official local launch, so confirm the battery version and warranty coverage before you buy.
Q) Does it come with a charger in the box?
A) That depends on where you buy it. Japan’s retail box includes a 100W charger, but Xiaomi’s global page says the general package excludes one. Check your local listing to be sure.
Q) How many software updates will it get?
A) Xiaomi promises six years of security updates in markets like Japan and Singapore, though it hasn’t confirmed how many major Android version upgrades you’ll get. The separate 72-month claim you may see refers to an internal ageing test, not a software update promise.
Q) How does the Pro Max compare to the Redmi Note 17 Pro?
A) The Pro Max has a faster Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chip, a bigger battery, and 100W charging. The Pro uses a Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 chip, an 8,340mAh battery, and 67W charging. Both share a similar 6.83-inch 1.5K display and the same 50MP plus 8MP rear camera setup.

articles.title: Astro Introduces Sätteri: A Rust-powered Markdown And Mdx Processor With Up To 60% Faster Builds
articles.text:
Sätteri, a new high-performance Markdown and MDX processor for the JavaScript ecosystem, has been introduced by the Astro team and now sits at the heart of the recently released Astro 7.0. Built in Rust and maintained separately by Astro core contributor Erika under the Bruits collective, Sätteri lives outside the Astro organisation but has become a core dependency of the framework, where the team says it contributes up to 60% faster builds.
Sätteri puts flexible JavaScript plugins on top of a fast Rust Markdown and MDX engine, using pulldown-cmark for CommonMark parsing and Oxc for MDX expression parsing. It ships platform-specific native binaries with a WASM fallback, the same approach Astro uses for its new Rust compiler, and it can be tried live in the browser via WebAssembly.
The processor first appeared as an opt-in @astrojs/markdown-satteri package in Astro 6.4, and Astro 7 promotes it to the default. The headline benefit is speed: switching the Astro and Cloudflare documentation sites to Sätteri shaved over a minute off each build, and overall Astro 7 builds improved by 15 to 61%. Much of that gain comes from moving parsing out of JavaScript, replacing the unified pipeline of remark, rehype and a long tail of dependencies that previously ran plugin after plugin over the full syntax tree.
Speed is not the only change. Sätteri implements natively many features that previously required separate plugins, including GitHub Flavored Markdown, smart punctuation, container directives, math, frontmatter, superscript, subscript and wikilinks. Optional features are enabled through the processor config.
On Hacker News, one developer expressed their disappointment:
Switch from widely supported unified/rehype to own rehype-incompatible markdown tooling just for build time speed improvement is quite upsetting
Good that they added a tool to keep using rehype, but I’m unsure that it will last
Which prompted a reply from Erika, the author of the library:
We don't intend on removing support for the unified ecosystem, we on purpose made the Markdown processing pipeline pluggable so that it was possible for both to exists!
The vast majority of our users don't use any sort of unified plugins, so a pipeline that's faster (and about 100 deps leaner) felt like a better default.
Another commenter asked:
How does Satteri compare to a standard library like marked (https://github.com/markedjs/marked)?
To which Erika also replied:
It depends in what regards you mean, I have some benchmarks here if you'd like to take a look at those:
https://github.com/Princesseuh/web-markdown-benchmark
The TL;DR is that marked is very light, but a bit on the slower side compared to Sätteri and markdown-it (and its forks). I'm not sure how friendly the extensibility is, but Sätteri re-use the same AST format as the unified ecosystem, which might feel more friendly.
Both good options, though!
The main migration caveat is that Sätteri does not run remark or rehype plugins. The Astro v7 upgrade guide advises that projects without plugins need no changes, while those depending on plugins can port them to Sätteri MDAST or HAST plugins or stay on unified by installing @astrojs/markdown-remark. Upgrades are handled with npx @astrojs/upgrade.
Sätteri is not alone in chasing native Markdown speed. Bun.markdown, written in Zig, has reported comparable gains but lacks a plugin system, leaving Sätteri's reuse of the unified AST format as a distinguishing feature. Sätteri is open source and available via npm and crates.io.

articles.title: Hyundai wants to sell humanoid and robot dogs through its car dealerships
articles.text:
Looking ahead: Imagine being able to swing by your local Hyundai dealership to buy a humanoid or dog-like robot. That scenario is the vision of the automaker's CEO, José Muñoz, and the company could even provide the financing for these expensive machines.
"We have existing potential distribution for selling robots through our dealer partners," said Muñoz during the company's investor day.
Back in 2021, Hyundai Motor Group took the surprising step of acquiring an 80% controlling stake in robotics giant Boston Dynamics, valuing the company at $1.1 billion.
Hyundai obviously wants a return on that investment. One of its recently announced plans is to build a factory capable of producing 30,000 Atlas humanoid robots annually by 2028. It wants to begin deploying the machines at its Georgia plant that same year, with plans to roll them out across all global production sites.
Then there's the quadrupedal Spot. It's had many jobs in its time: a bomb squad observation device, cleaner and gardener, guard dog, military assistant, pizza delivery/seagull fighter, factory inspector, and more. It was also tested as a package delivery assistant for a second time in July. Meanwhile, Hyundai has used Spot robots at its facilities for inspections and maintenance.
There's also Stretch, a warehouse-focused robot that's essentially an arm on a movable base.
These robots aren't cheap. Spot previously started at $74,500, but it's likely a lot more expensive these days (buyers have to contact the company for a quote). Advanced humanoid bots, especially those designed for commercial tasks, are even pricier. That could be why Muñoz said Hyundai Capital, which finances cars, is looking at ways of doing the same for robots, though it's unclear whether Muñoz was referring to enterprise customers or a future consumer market.
Hyundai isn't the only automaker moving into this space. Tesla is refitting part of its Fremont facility to build Optimus, which Elon Musk wants to deploy within the company before selling it to others. BMW has already used Figure 02 at its South Carolina plant; the humanoid supported production of more than 30,000 X3 vehicles during a ten-month trial. Mercedes-Benz, meanwhile, is testing Apptronik's Apollo in its factories.
For now, factories and warehouses are the machines' most realistic commercial settings. Stretch is unloading trucks for logistics firms such as DHL and Maersk, while Amazon and GXO have trialed Agility Robotics' Digit for repetitive container-moving work.
Companies always repeat the same old line about robots taking exhausting or dangerous jobs and filling labor shortages rather than replacing people, but workers have reason to worry. A machine capable of running long shifts without wages, holidays, or sick leave is always going to pose a threat to its fleshy counterparts. Whether consumers ever buy Atlas alongside an Ioniq remains to be seen, but commercial robots are already clocking in.

articles.title: Suivez en direct le vol d'Ariane 6, en route vers une orbite que la fusée n'a jamais atteinte
articles.text:
Mise à jour : dernière ligne droite pour le décollage, la météo est au vert.
Le 27 août 2026, Ariane 6 vise pour la première fois l’orbite de transfert géostationnaire. Avec déjà huit vols au compteur, le lanceur européen s’attaque à la destination qui a fait toute la carrière commerciale d’Ariane 5. Voici le programme de ce tir inédit pour ce lanceur, à suivre en direct ce soir, et en streaming.
Après avoir volé cette année dans sa version la plus puissante, à quatre boosters, Ariane 6 poursuit sa série de premières en 2026. L’objectif du jour : envoyer une charge utile à 36 000 km de la Terre, au-dessus de l’équateur, sur cette orbite qui nous paraît immobile depuis le plancher des vaches.
Le 9e vol d’Ariane 6 en résumé
- Quoi ? Le 9e décollage d’Ariane 6 (mission VA270) et le premier ciblant l’orbite de transfert géostationnaire ;
- Quand ? Le 27 août 2026, avec une fenêtre de tir s’ouvrant à 22h10 (heure de Paris) ;
- Où ? Depuis le Centre spatial guyanais, pour une mise en orbite à 36 000 km d’altitude ;
- Que verra-t-on ? Le décollage de la version Ariane 62, son ascension et le largage du satellite météorologique européen MTG-I2.
Où voir le lancement d’Ariane 6 en direct ?
Arianespace assurera une retransmission vidéo de cet événement. Le flux officiel démarrera à 21h45, heure de Paris, soit un peu moins d’une demi-heure avant le top départ. Vous pourrez suivre l’édition spéciale directement sur les canaux et réseaux sociaux de l’entreprise. Un flux vidéo est proposé juste en dessous également :
Quelle est la mission VA270 ?
Pour ce neuvième vol, Arianespace déploie la configuration « légère » de sa fusée, dite Ariane 62, équipée de deux boosters à poudre P120C.
Sous la coiffe se trouve MTG-I2, un satellite météorologique construit par Thales Alenia Space pour EUMETSAT. Sa tâche consistera à balayer le continent européen toutes les deux minutes et demie afin de repérer très tôt les orages violents ou anticiper les inondations.
MTG-I2 ne partira pas seul dans le ciel : il vient compléter la première famille des satellites Météosat Troisième Génération. Il fonctionnera en tandem avec MTG-I1, déjà en poste depuis son lancement par une Ariane 5 en décembre 2022, pour assurer la continuité du service d’observation au-dessus de l’Europe.
Mais le véritable enjeu de cette mission dépasse la météo. Il réside dans sa destination. Si Ariane 6 s’est jusqu’à présent illustrée en orbite basse (constellation Leo d’Amazon) et moyenne (satellites Galileo), elle n’avait pas encore visé l’orbite de transfert géostationnaire (GTO).
C’est sur ce terrain de jeu historique qu’Ariane 5 a forgé son excellente réputation, en y déployant plus de 170 satellites avec une fiabilité quasi parfaite en 27 ans. En retrouvant cette orbite haute, Arianespace espère valider définitivement Ariane 6 sur le créneau crucial des lourds satellites de télécommunications face à SpaceX, et garantir l’accès autonome de l’Europe à l’espace.
Quand décolle la fusée Ariane 6 ?
La fenêtre de tir s’ouvrira ce soir, le 27 août 2026, à 22h10 (heure de Paris). En cas d’imprévu météorologique ou technique, Arianespace dispose d’une marge de deux heures et demie pour procéder au lancement. Le vol en lui-même sera expéditif : comptez seulement 36 minutes entre l’arrachement au pas de tir et le largage final du satellite.

articles.title: GTA 6 sur Netflix et YouTube : voici où regarder l'aperçu de 26 minutes — Frandroid
articles.text:
Rarement (voire jamais) un jeu a-t-il été aussi attendu que GTA 6. Alors que la sortie du titre reste prévue le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series et que les précommandes sont ouvertes depuis fin juin, Rockstar a enfin diffusé son aperçu étendu en exclusivité sur Netflix, ce jeudi 27 août à 21 heures (heure de Paris). Une vidéo de 26 minutes et 49 secondes, intégralement capturée sur une PS5 standard, qui a d’ailleurs fait plier les serveurs de Netflix dès les premières minutes.
Gaming ou études, pourquoi choisir ? Équipement tech, PC et écrans : profitez de jusqu’à -40 % pour la rentrée chez PcComponentes ! Livraison offerte dès 50 € et garantie remplacement 24 h jusqu’au 12 septembre.
GTA 6 : l’aperçu large commenté en direct
Nous savons à quoi ressemblera le jeu de la décennie !
Nous venons de réagir à chaud sur les 26 minutes de gameplay de GTA 6 diffusés en avant-première sur Netflix ! Nous savons désormais à quoi ressemblera la prochaine pépite de Rockstar et nous vous proposons ici un plus ample décryptage de cette séquence qui fait et fera encore couler beaucoup d’encre.
Clap de fin !
Et c’est sur un cliffhanger de la mission et sur de somptueuses images de Leonida que prend fin cet aperçu étendu de GTA 6 ! Nous n’avons pas assez abordé les différentes mécaniques de gameplay, de la possibilité de passer de Jason à Lucia (comme dans GTA 5) à la compétence bullet time de Jason, tant il y avait à voir.
Aucune grosse annonce de Rockstar en fin de vidéo. GTA 6 est toujours prévu pour le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Nous vous disons dans cet article où précommander le jeu de la décennie au meilleur prix.
Plus que 5 minutes !
Nous en sommes aux cinq dernières minutes de l’aperçu étendu et on peut dire que nous en prenons plein les yeux jusqu’ici. Pour cette dernière séquence, Rockstar nous montre les images d’une mission dans laquelle Jason et Lucia, en tenue chic, doivent protéger une huile de Leonida.
L’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 fait aussi tomber Twitch !
Netflix a lâché en premier, Twitch n’a pas tardé à suivre. Sans surprise, des milliers de streams en simultané, certains à plus de 6 000 spectateurs, tous branchés sur le même flux Netflix déjà en surchauffe. Selon les signalements relayés sur les réseaux sociaux, l’accès aux chaînes et au chat a été perturbé pendant la première demi-heure de diffusion. Twitch n’a pas communiqué officiellement sur une panne à l’heure où on écrit ces lignes, mais Downdetector montre un vrai pic de signalements.
Encore des nouveautés !
Le derniers tiers de l’aperçu étendu dévoile encore plus de nouveautés alors jamais aperçues dans aucun GTA : balade en hydroglisseur dans les marécages ou en kayak, séance de musculation à la salle de sport, baignade avec les dauphins, rallye automobile, soirée dans un club de strip-tease. Il y aura même de la plongée sous-marine !
Le niveau de recherche six étoiles est de retour !
Disparu depuis GTA : San Andreas, le niveau de recherche six étoiles fera bien son grand retour sur GTA 6 comme le révèle l’aperçu étendu.
Troisième partie de l’aperçu étendu
L’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 est un peu fourre-tout, alternant entre phases de plusieurs minutes de gameplay, cinématiques et succession de scènes de deux secondes. Après la partie rooftop, Rockstar nous dévoile des images de course-poursuite automobile (et avec des hélicos) et de fusillade avec le joueur dans la peau de Jason tirant sur les poursuivants depuis l’arrière d’une voiture.
D’autres éléments de gameplay en images
Juste avant la sortie de l’aperçu étendu, Rockstar teasait quelques éléments de gameplay que nous pouvons ici voir en images. Des actions anodines telles que « fumer », « manger » et « se tenir la main » qui auraient des conséquences sur l’hygiène de vie et la relation entre les personnages. Reste à savoir si ces actions auraient des conséquences plus fortes comme réduire l’endurance du personnage et même avoir des répercussions sur le scénario.
En voiture Jason !
Première virée en voiture avec notre couple de gangsters, l’occasion d’apercevoir la faune automobile et la circulation chaotique comme dans tout bon Grand Theft Auto. Des images éparses de gameplay se succèdent ensuite : combats de rue, et de ring, fusillades et sorties sur rooftop.
Deuxième partie de l’aperçu étendu
Après une phase de fusillade bien sentie dans la résidence, on passe à une ambiance beaucoup plus chill dans l’appartement de Jason et Lucia. Vous serez peut-être heureux d’apprendre qu’il sera possible de se poser devant la télé une bière bien fraîche entre les mains.
L’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 fait planter Netflix
Quelques minutes ont suffi. La plateforme a fléchi sous l’afflux de curieux, et Downdetector a enregistré une flambée de signalements de panne au moment même de la mise en ligne. À 20h58, quasiment 1 400 signalements ont été recensés.
PS5 ou PS5 Pro ?
Graphiquement, c’est très propre et bien que niveau fluidité on sent que nous ne sommes pas sur du 120 FPS, on se demande sur quelle PlayStation 5 le gameplay a-t-il été capturé. PS5 Slim ou PS5 Pro ? Une idée ?
Premier aperçu du HUD
Nous avons un premier aperçu du HUD de GTA 6 avec une interface très similaire à celle de Red Dead Redemption 2 avec les commandes d’action indiquées en bas à droite de l’écran. Un système d’honneur serait possiblement présent, Jason semble avoir gagné des sortes de points après avoir caressé un chien.
C’est tout noir !
Malheureusement, impossible de vous montrer ne serait-ce que des captures d’écran du gameplay, le contenu étant protégé par DRM. Les sous-titres restent toutefois visibles.
GTA 6, les premières images in-game
Les premières images de l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 nous mettent dans la peau de Jason, accompagné de Lucia, dans une résidence vraisemblablement contrôlée par un gang. Impression à chaud : techniquement, ça a l’air très prometteur, d’un point de vue graphique mais aussi s’agissant de l’animation des PNJ.
KO technique
Après un petit souci technique pile à 21 heures (sûrement les serveurs de Netflix qui ont prix un coup), l’aperçu étendu peut enfin être visionné.
C’est parti pour l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 !
L’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 est en ligne sur Netflix ! Sur Frandroid, nous allons passer la soirée à commenter en live les 26 minutes de gameplay du nouveau titre de Rockstar. Vaudra-t-il les 13 ans d’attente après GTA V ? Doit-on s’attendre à une grosse annonce ce soir ? Découvrons sans plus attendre l’État de Leonida dans la peau de Jason et Lucia !
Plus que 30 minutes !
Encore une demi-heure avant la publication de l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 sur Netflix ! Selon les dernières informations, l’extrait durera 26 minutes et sera entièrement composé d’images in-game capturées sur PlayStation 5.
Rendez-vous à 21 heures sur Netflix
L’aperçu étendu de GTA 6 sera diffusé à partir de 21 heures sur Netflix. Ici, sur Frandroid, on va passer un bout de notre soirée à commenter la vidéo et notamment les informations intéressantes qui s’en dégagent !
Ce que montre l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6
Cette vidéo, qu’on peut considérer comme le troisième trailer de GTA 6, arrive gratuitement sur YouTube vers 3 heures du matin (heure de Paris), en 4K, à la fin des six heures d’exclusivité Netflix. Elle tient ses promesses côté images de gameplay : un deal qui dérape, des braquages, une fusillade en soirée mondaine, Vice City de nuit, et un système de police qui retient votre tenue et votre véhicule. On a analysé les 27 minutes scène par scène dans un article dédié. Rockstar avait prévenu que GTA 6 donnerait beaucoup d’importance aux conséquences de vos choix, et le « profil criminel » aperçu dans la vidéo le confirme.
    À lire aussi : 
    GTA 6 sur Netflix : ce que révèlent vraiment les 27 minutes de gameplay
Si vous n’avez pas d’abonnement Netflix, nos commentaires et informations à chaud, tirés de ce fameux aperçu large de GTA 6, sont à retrouver ci-dessous pour patienter jusqu’à la fin de l’exclusivité temporaire de la plateforme SVoD. Et si la vidéo vous a convaincu, on a réuni les meilleures offres de précommande, avec un prix de départ à 79,99 euros pour l’édition standard.

articles.title: Samsung announces a slew of world's first OLED monitors at Gamescom, including the highest refresh rate we've ever seen
articles.text:
Samsung just blew me away at Gamescom with its ridiculously-fast 1100Hz OLED monitor
Will anyone be able to afford the hardware to hit those refresh rates?
Samsung took to its own stage at Gamescom today to announce a slew of new Odyssey OLED gaming screens for 2027, including some very tasty world firsts.
Top of the new range is the Odyssey OLED G6 G60H, which boasts a 1440p Fast IPS panel, complete with a 600Hz refresh rate.
If that ridiculous refresh speed isn't enough, you can dial down the resolution to HD and benefit from 1100Hz, making this Samsung screen the fastest we've ever seen in that respect.
It also features AMD FreeSync Premium Pro VRR and is Nvidia G-Sync compatible.
If you want something bigger, the Odyssey OLED G7 marks the world's first 42-inch curved gaming screen in a classic 16:9 aspect ratio. It's a 4K OLED panel with up to a 165Hz refresh rate and an aggressive 1000R curve for an immersive finish.
For reference, Samsung says the G7 is some 72% larger than a typical 32-inch curved panel in its range for greater immersion, so it can fill even more of your field of vision.
Bigger and better?
The new Odyssey OLED G8 is stacked with cool-sounding features – a 32-inch 4K tandem OLED with a 360Hz refresh rate that features Samsung's latest fifth-gen QD-OLED panel with its Penta Tandem tech and an RGB stripe sub-pixel layout for greater power efficiency, longevity, and sharper text.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The G8 also supports 'triple mode', so 4K/360hz isn't your only option. Drop down to 1440p, and the screen yields a 520Hz refresh rate. Or, if that's not enough, then Full HD output at 680Hz is possible.
Port-wise, Samsung has kitted it out with DP 2.1 UHBR20, two HDMI 2.1 ports, a USB-C with up to 98W of power delivery, plus a USB hub with two downstream ports and KVM support.
For ultrawide fans, the new Odyssey OLED G9 offers a 49-inch panel with a 5120 x 1440 resolution and up to 360Hz. It also has dual-mode power with 720Hz at 'dual HD' (2560 x 720) and a fifth-gen QD-OLED panel with Penta Tandem tech.
Samsung says the Odyssey OLED G9 offers up to 1300 nits of peak brightness at a 4K resolution in a 3% window for some punchy output.
Alongside the slew of new screens, it also reaffirmed its commitment to glasses-free 3D tech, with wider support mentioned for some of the biggest titles and the presence of HDR10+ gaming in some big releases, including the new Call of Duty, and upwards of 20 games supporting the standard by the first half of 2027.

Reece Bithrey is a freelance journalist with credits in Trusted Reviews, Digital Foundry, PC Gamer, TechRadar, PCGamesN, and Custom PC magazine reviewing all sorts of computing gubbins, including keyboards, mice, laptops, and more. He also has his own blog, UNTITLED, has bylines for WatchGecko's online magazine, and graduated from the University of Leeds with a degree in International History and Politics in 2023. When not writing, you'll usually find him bellowing at virtual footballers on Football Manager or tinkering with mechanical keyboards.

articles.title: iPhone 16 (256 GB) tem maior queda de preço dos últimos meses com cupom • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone 16 (256 GB) tem maior queda de preço dos últimos meses com cupom
iPhone 16 tem tela OLED de 120 Hz e câmeras de 48 MP; celular da Apple recebe desconto de 43% no Pix combinado com cupom válido somente hoje
O iPhone 16 de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 4.859 no Pix com cupom COMPRABOA no Mercado Livre. O celular da Apple com tela OLED, chip A18 e câmera wide de 48 MP alcança o menor preço desde junho de 2026 com desconto de 43% sobre o original de R$ 6.599, mas a promoção só é válida nesta quinta-feira (27).
Apesar de ter sido lançado em 2024, o iPhone 16 permanece como um dos melhores celulares da Apple. Seu kit de câmeras traz uma wide com OIS de 48 MP e uma ultrawide de 12 MP com ângulo de 120º, que capturam belas cenas em ambientes amplos, e uma frontal de 12 MP que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K.
O chip Apple A18 e os 8 GB de RAM permitem rodar apps pesados em multitarefa, games e funções da suíte Apple Intelligence localmente. Os 256 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço interno razoável para guardar fotos e vídeos.
Sua tela LPTO Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″ possui brilho de até 2.000 nits e oferece reprodução de imagens com cores vibrantes, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield protege o display em ocorrências do dia a dia, como eventuais quedas e pancadas.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 16 recebe a certificação IP68, que confere proteção adicional em cenários como ambientes empoeirados e mergulhos acidentais, oferecendo assim durabilidade prolongada ao aparelho.
Sua bateria de 3.561 mAh possui autonomia de até 22 horas de reprodução de vídeo segundo a Apple, além de suportar MagSafe e carregamento rápido de 25 W via USB-C. Dessa forma, o usuário não precisa se preocupar em ficar sem energia durante o curso de um dia movimentado.
O iPhone 16 de 256 GB (R$ 4.859 no Pix com cupom COMPRABOA) foi atualizado para o iOS 26 e deve receber pelo menos mais quatro atualizações do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple ainda conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.3 e possui NFC via Apple Pay.

articles.title: Rockstar Responds to GTA VI Leaks After Legal Actions Fail
articles.text:
Thursday, August 27th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Rockstar Responds to GTA VI Leaks After Legal Actions Fail
Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company and publisher of Grand Theft Auto VI, previously responded to the detailed leaks from Cyberleek by issuing subpoenas to Microsoft and Discord in order to identify and track down the anonymous leaker, although that doesn't seem to have helped, since the Cyberleek leaks have continued unabated. Following the legal route, Rockstar Games has publicly addressed the leaks in a recent post on X, stating that the leaks are "heartbreaking" to the team, and apologizing for the game's extended development time frame. 
The leaks shared by Cyberleek revealed much of the studio's closely held secrets about GTA VI, including some of the game's mechanics, the full map, driving and vehicle designs, as well as a number of NPC interactions, and, although there was doubt about the authenticity of the leaks, Rockstar and Take-Two addressing the leaks serves to lend credence to the leaker's claims. Rockstar says in the statement about the leaks that it hopes that "everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19."The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to have a massive ripple effect on the gaming industry at large, with everyone from indie game developers and peripherals makers expecting changes in consumer buying patterns around November 2026 when GTA VI is slated to launch.
The full statement by Rockstar Games follows.
Dear all, 
		
		Source:
				Rockstar Games			
	
	
	
		
	
		
The leaks shared by Cyberleek revealed much of the studio's closely held secrets about GTA VI, including some of the game's mechanics, the full map, driving and vehicle designs, as well as a number of NPC interactions, and, although there was doubt about the authenticity of the leaks, Rockstar and Take-Two addressing the leaks serves to lend credence to the leaker's claims. Rockstar says in the statement about the leaks that it hopes that "everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19."The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to have a massive ripple effect on the gaming industry at large, with everyone from indie game developers and peripherals makers expecting changes in consumer buying patterns around November 2026 when GTA VI is slated to launch.
The full statement by Rockstar Games follows.
Dear all, 
We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has—from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know.
We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19.
We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week—your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games.
We look forward to sharing more with you soon.
Sincerely, Rockstar Games

articles.title: Cada vez más países ven publicidad en ChatGPT: India es entra a esta etapa de monetización con Europa y EE.UU.
articles.text:
La publicidad en ChatGPT está cada vez más presente en diferentes países. OpenAI ha iniciado el despliegue de anuncios en India y en más de 30 países europeos, expandiendo un modelo que ya había empezado en Estados Unidos.
Este movimiento supone un cambio importante en la experiencia de millones de usuarios, que ahora deberán ver anuncios para seguir usando la aplicación de manera gratuita.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo funcionará el sistema de anuncios en ChatGPT
La implementación de ChatGPT Ads está diseñada para aparecer exclusivamente en los planes gratuitos y de bajo coste, denominados Free y Go. Los usuarios que hayan optado por suscripciones de pago superiores —Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise y Education— seguirán disfrutando de una experiencia libre de publicidad.
Esta diferenciación busca mantener el atractivo de los servicios premium y ofrece a los anunciantes acceso a grandes volúmenes de usuarios activos.
Los anuncios se mostrarán a adultos que hayan iniciado sesión en la plataforma, quedando excluidos los menores de 18 años y cualquier contexto sensible, como consultas sobre salud mental o política. La inserción publicitaria se ubicará debajo de las respuestas del asistente, siempre identificada de forma clara y separada visualmente de los contenidos generados por la IA.
PUBLICIDAD
OpenAI subraya que los anuncios no influyen en las respuestas del sistema y que los anunciantes no podrán acceder a las conversaciones, historiales ni datos personales de los usuarios.
La experiencia publicitaria estará guiada por cinco principios: independencia de las respuestas, privacidad de las conversaciones, control y elección del usuario, alineación con la misión de ampliar el acceso a la IA, y una apuesta por el valor a largo plazo que prioriza la confianza y la calidad sobre los ingresos inmediatos. Los usuarios podrán descartar los anuncios, gestionar la personalización y borrar sus datos asociados.
PUBLICIDAD
A qué tipo de usuarios se mostrarán los anuncios
El despliegue de la publicidad en ChatGPT afecta a quienes utilizan las versiones gratuitas o de bajo coste, es decir, los segmentos más numerosos y activos. En India, por ejemplo, OpenAI estima que más de 100 millones de usuarios semanales emplean ChatGPT, la mayoría en los planes Free y Go.
Las suscripciones Plus y Pro, que sumaban ya 35 millones de usuarios pagos a fines de 2025, así como las variantes Business, Enterprise y Education, seguirán sin publicidad, en línea con el modelo adoptado por otras grandes plataformas digitales.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de India, la llegada del sistema de anuncios coincide con el lanzamiento de un gestor de campañas denominado Ads Manager, que estará disponible a partir del 4 de septiembre.
Esta plataforma permitirá a empresas y anunciantes de todos los tamaños crear y administrar sus campañas con un presupuesto diario mínimo de 725 rupías ($7,60 dóalres).
PUBLICIDAD
Países donde se implementa el sistema de publicidad de ChatGPT
Después de su estreno en Estados Unidos, OpenAI ha extendido ChatGPT Ads primero a India y, desde el 24 de agosto, a 30 países europeos, incluyendo Alemania, España, Francia y Bélgica.
El despliegue europeo se realiza en colaboración con agencias como Publicis, WPP, Omnicom, MediaPlus, Havas y Dentsu. Con este paso, OpenAI alinea su modelo de negocio al de gigantes como Google y Meta, donde la publicidad es el motor principal de financiación de servicios gratuitos.
PUBLICIDAD
El acceso al Ads Manager en India permitirá que empresas nacionales y multinacionales se sumen a la plataforma, facilitando la entrada de marcas emergentes y pequeños negocios. En Europa, los anuncios estarán disponibles para los anunciantes a través de las agencias mencionadas.
En todos los casos, OpenAI insiste en que la publicidad no comprometerá la privacidad ni la experiencia central de ChatGPT, y que el sistema irá evolucionando a partir del aprendizaje y la retroalimentación de los usuarios y anunciantes.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa prevé introducir nuevos formatos y opciones de compra, siempre bajo el compromiso de mantener una separación clara entre los anuncios y las respuestas generadas por la IA.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: 100.000 neue Welten: So blockiert Nasas neues Teleskop störendes Sternenlicht
articles.text:
Nasa: Nancy-Grace-Roman-Teleskop soll Sternenlicht blockieren, um 100.000 Exoplaneten zu finden
Es ist im SpaceX-Hangar angekommen – somit ist das Nancy-Roman-Weltraumteleskop bereit für seinen Start am Sonntag, den 30. August 2026 vom Kennedy Space Center in Florida. An Bord einer Falcon-Heavy-Rakete soll es dann neun Monate früher als geplant ins All gehen. Das Ziel soll der Lagrange-Punkt 2 sein. Von dort aus wollen Wissenschaftler:innen das Teleskop nutzen, um dem Weltraum weitere Geheimnisse zu entlocken. Dazu hat es maßgeschneiderte Instrumente dabei und könnte ganz nebenbei auch einen Beitrag zur Asteroiden-Abwehr liefern. Hauptsächlich aber wird das 10,5 Tonnen schwere Observatorium den ersten „aktiven“ Koronagrafen im Weltraum mitführen. Dieser kann bei der Aufnahme den Großteil des Lichts eines Sterns effektiv ausblenden. Dadurch können Astronom:innen erstmals Bilder von Planeten aufnehmen, die andere Sterne umkreisen und damit denen in unserem Sonnensystem ähneln. Dies könnte den Weg für eine zukünftige Mission ebnen, die die ersten Fotos von erdähnlichen Welten liefert.
„Ich hoffe, dass das Projekt als entscheidender Meilenstein für die Suche nach einer Erde 2.0 in Erinnerung bleibt“, sagt Brandon Creager, leitender technischer Ingenieur für das Instrument am Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) der Nasa. Benannt nach Nancy Grace Roman, der ersten Chefin der Astronomieabteilung der Nasa, verfügt das neue Weltraumteleskop über eine Wide-Field-Kamera mit rund 300 Megapixel. Sie soll Bilder aufnehmen, die etwa 100 Mal größer sind als Langzeitbelichtungsaufnahmen des Vorgängers Hubble bei ähnlichen Auflösungen.
Exoplaneten mit Nancy-Grace-Roman-Weltraumteleskop entdecken
Diese Fähigkeit wird Astronom:innen dabei helfen, die Natur von dunkler Materie und dunkler Energie zu entschlüsseln, hoffen die Forschenden. Rund 100.000 neue Exoplaneten sollen entdeckt werden, also Planeten außerhalb unseres Sonnensystems. Deren Existenz lässt sich aus der Art und Weise ableiten, wie sie das Licht weiter entfernter Sterne verzerren. Javier Viaña, Wissenschaftler an der Harvard-Universität, dessen zwei Projekte für das hart umkämpfte erste Beobachtungsjahr des Teleskops ausgewählt wurden, vergleicht diesen Sprung mit dem „Befragen einer Handvoll Menschen“ hin zur „Durchführung einer weltweiten Volkszählung“.
Eine weitere Kamera wird den Koronagrafen direkt nutzen, der das Licht eines Sterns ausblendet, während jeweils ein Sternsystem beobachtet wird. Das Instrument soll Forschenden einen beispiellosen Einblick in den Bereich um einen Stern herum ermöglichen und es ihnen erlauben, kleinere, lichtschwächere, näher gelegene Exoplaneten zu erkennen. „Es gibt uns die Möglichkeit, Planeten zu sehen, die wir bisher physisch nicht wahrnehmen konnten“, sagt Creager.
Anders als Hubble und James-Webb: Sternenlicht unterdrücken anstatt ausblenden
Koronagrafen im Weltraum sind eigentlich nichts Neues. Frühere Versionen, wie sie derzeit an Bord des Hubble-Teleskops und des James-Webb-Weltraumteleskops zum Einsatz kommen, nutzen jedoch ein stationäres System, um das Licht eines Sterns auszublenden. Dieser Ansatz hilft zwar, gleicht aber ein wenig dem Versuch, mit dem Daumen die Taschenlampe abzudecken, während man in einem dunklen Raum nach einem Glühwürmchen sucht. Zwar verschwindet das Licht der Lampe, doch Streulicht kann entweichen und das Licht des Insekts überstrahlen.
In einem Teleskop kann diese Blendung von Licht stammen, das an den Rändern der Geräte austritt – oder von winzigen Unvollkommenheiten in Spiegeln und Beschichtungen, die das Sternenlicht fleckenförmig streuen können. All dies kann einen Planeten unsichtbar machen oder sogar seine Spuren vortäuschen.
Der Koronagraf am Roman-Teleskop wird jedoch etwas versuchen, was bei solchen Anlagen bis zu diesem Jahr noch völlig unbekannt war: Vor jeder Beobachtung wird er das Restlicht messen und versuchen, es zu unterdrücken – eine Technik, die als aktive Wellenfrontkontrolle bekannt ist. Das Teleskop ist dazu in der Lage, weil es zwei verformbare Spiegel enthält. Jeder verfügt über ein Schachbrettmuster aus Aktuatoren unter einer dünnen, verformbaren Glasscheibe. Durch geringe Spannungen ziehen sich die Aktuatoren zusammen und schieben ihre Spiegelabschnitte leicht nach hinten. Ein wenig so, als würden Tausende mikroskopisch kleiner Finger die Oberfläche vorsichtig formen.
Versteckte Exoplaneten werden durch absorbierte Photonen sichtbar
Der Effekt ist sehr subtil: Jeder Spiegelbereich kann sich um bis zu 0,5 Mikrometer verformen – das entspricht etwa einem Viertel der Größe eines E.-coli-Bakteriums. Die Schritte betragen dabei jeweils nur etwa 10 Pikometer. Das ist etwa ein Zehntel des Durchmessers eines Wasserstoffatoms, sagt Ilya Poberezhskiy, Systemingenieur für das Teleskop am JPL. Die Aktuatoren ermöglichen es den Spiegeln, eine „aktive Wellenfront“ zu erzeugen, bei der jede Komponente in die perfekte Position bewegt wird, um einfallende Wellen unerwünschten Lichts auszugleichen – ein bisschen wie bei einem Kopfhörer mit Geräuschunterdrückung, nur für Licht statt für Schall. Das „gelöschte“ Licht erzeugt einen „donutförmigen Bereich um den Stern herum, in dem wir das Sternenlicht unterdrücken und in dem wir hoffen, Exoplaneten zu finden“, sagt Poberezhskiy.
Im Vergleich zu aktuellen Weltraum-Koronagrafen soll das System die Empfindlichkeit gegenüber Exoplaneten um bis zum Faktor 1.000 verbessern und so Planeten sichtbar machen, die sonst nicht zum Vorschein kommen würden. Wie Hubble und JWST nutzt auch das Roman-Teleskop sogenannte Masken – strukturierte Platten, die im Lichtweg platziert werden und dazu dienen, die auftreffenden Photonen abzublocken. Ein Werkzeug im Maskenarsenal des Roman-Teleskops ist eine Art von „Siliziumgras“, ein Dickicht aus mikroskopisch kleinen Stacheln auf einigen der Masken, das in bestimmten Konfigurationen eingesetzt werden kann. Es absorbiert Photonen, damit diese nicht im Teleskop hin und her schießen und versehentlich einen Detektor erreichen.
Jupiter ähnliche Planeten mit Nancy-Grace-Roman-Weltraumteleskop aufspüren
Das in diesen Siliziumwald eintretende Licht wird immer tiefer zwischen den Stacheln hin- und hergeworfen und bleibt dort gefangen, anstatt zur Kamera reflektiert zu werden. „Sobald das Licht dort hineinkommt, kommt es nie wieder heraus“, sagt Poberezhskiy. Die Spiegel und Masken bilden eine Abfolge von Toren und „Hecken“, um so viel wie möglich von dem erhaltenen Planetenlicht zum endgültigen Detektor zu leiten. Diese aufwendige Anordnung könnte ein neues Kapitel in der direkten Abbildung von Exoplaneten ermöglichen.
Fast alle bisher fotografierten Exoplaneten sind überdimensionale Himmelskörper, die den Planeten unseres Sonnensystems in nichts ähneln: Sie haben ein Vielfaches der Masse des Jupiters, glühen noch immer von der Restwärme ihrer Entstehung und umkreisen ihren Stern zehn- oder hundertmal weiter entfernt als die Erde die Sonne. Ihre Bedeutung liegt darin, dass sie relativ leicht zu erkennen sind. Ihre Größe, ihre Wärme und ihre Entfernung vom Mutterstern lassen sie im Infrarotlicht hell leuchten, weit entfernt von der stärksten Blendung durch ihren Stern.
Das Roman-Teleskop könnte jedoch ein echtes Jupiter-Analogon direkt abbilden – einen Planeten, der in seiner Masse dem Jupiter ähnelt und einen sonnenähnlichen Stern umkreist, der einige wenige Male weiter entfernt ist als die Erde von unserer Sonne. Im Gegensatz zu den „heißen Jupitern“, die wir derzeit beobachten können, wäre dieser ein viel reiferer Gasriese wie der unsere, der nach Milliarden von Jahren der Abkühlung hauptsächlich das Licht seines Muttersterns reflektiert – anstatt selbst starkes Licht auszustrahlen. Astronomen konnten die Existenz solcher Planeten bisher aus der Gravitationsschwankung ableiten, die sie dem Stern verleihen.
Das Roman-Teleskop hingegen wird das vom Planeten selbst reflektierte Sternenlicht erfassen. „Wir betrachten nicht den Stern und auch nicht die Auswirkungen des Planeten auf den Stern“, sagt Meredith MacGregor, Professorin für Astronomie an der Johns Hopkins University, die sich ebenfalls einen Platz im Beobachtungsprogramm gesichert hat. „Wir beobachten tatsächlich den Planeten selbst, und das ist unglaublich mächtig.“
Sobald dieses Instrument zur Verfügung steht, sind die Wissenschaftler:innen an der Reihe, ihre Arbeit zu verrichten. „Ich habe ehrlich gesagt etwas Angst davor, wie wir alle damit umgehen werden, denn ich glaube, es sind einfach so viele Daten“, sagt MacGregor. „Ich denke, die Leute werden noch jahrzehntelang an den Roman-Daten arbeiten.“ Man sollte jedoch nicht erwarten, in den kommenden Monaten ein 4K-Foto eines außerirdischen Jupiters zu sehen. Roman wird nicht in der Lage sein, einen solchen Planeten als klar erkennbaren Globus abzubilden – bestenfalls wird er wahrscheinlich einer Ansammlung von Pixeln ähneln.
Dennoch wird das ausreichen, sagt MacGregor, da Roman dann mithilfe des Koronagrafen Informationen über die verschiedenen Wellenlängen des vom Planeten ausgestrahlten Lichts gewinnen kann. Die geben den Astronomen Aufschluss über dessen atmosphärische Chemie. „Man nimmt etwas, das nur ein Lichtpunkt ist, und verwandelt es in eine echte Welt“, sagt sie, „denn wenn man das über seine Atmosphäre weiß, weiß man nun auch etwas über die Oberfläche des Planeten und die Möglichkeit, dass es auf diesem Planeten Leben gibt, oder? Das ist also ein großer Schritt.“
Ergebnisse für das Habitable Worlds Observatory
Während der ersten Beobachtungen werden Wissenschaftler:innen und Ingenieur:innen prüfen, ob es ihnen gelingt, einen Stern genau im Zentrum der Masken des Koronagrafen zu halten, die Spiegel auszurichten, den dunklen „Donut“ (wie Poberezhskiy ihn beschreibt) zu „graben“ und dann alles stabil zu halten, während sich das Raumfahrzeug durch den Weltraum bewegt und sich die Temperatur aktiv ändert.
Die Ergebnisse werden in das von der Nasa vorgeschlagene „Habitable Worlds Observatory“ einfließen – den Traum vieler Exoplaneten-Astronomen –, das theoretisch in der Lage sein wird, das Licht eines erdähnlichen Planeten von dem eines sonnenähnlichen Sterns zu trennen, der über 10 Milliarden Mal heller ist. Creager, der seit 2018 an dem Instrument arbeitet, ist stolz auf diese Leistung: „Nicht viele Menschen können sagen: ‚Ich habe etwas gebaut, und es macht ein Bild von einem Planeten, der sich bei einem Stern befindet, der 50 oder 100 Lichtjahre entfernt ist.‘“ Er stellt sich den Moment vor, in dem er und sein Team das erste Bild betrachten können, sobald es eintrifft: „Ja, das haben wir geschafft.“

articles.title: 'GTA 6': estas son las canciones que suenan en el nuevo vistazo extendido
articles.text:
El vistazo extendido a GTA 6 ya se encuentra disponible en Netflix y en cuestión de horas se publicará también en YouTube. El nuevo material de Rockstar Games no solo nos ha permitido disfrutar de una puesta en escena espectacular, con una historia y un gameplay realmente prometedores, sino que también nos ha entregado una gran cantidad de música que merece la pena destacar.
Durante los 26 minutos de duración del material nos hemos topado con muchas canciones, y no queremos dejar escapar la oportunidad de mencionarla. Si el efecto GTA 6 de los primeros tráilers se repite, seguramente muchas de estas verán dispararse sus reproducciones en plataformas como YouTube, Spotify y Apple Music. Los casos de Love is a long road, de Tom Petty, y Hot Togheter, de The Pointers Sisters, son un antecedente bastante prometedor para los artistas que han licenciado su música al juego.
A continuación, compartiremos el listado con las canciones que aparecen en el vistazo extendido de GTA 6. Es posible que se nos haya escapado alguna, pero tratamos de recopilar las más notorias. Como puedes imaginar, hay un poco de todo y para todos los gustos: desde hip hop, rap, música latina, rock y pop, hasta una balada inolvidable de Phil Collins sonando como música de elevador.
Las canciones que suenan en el nuevo vistazo extendido a GTA 6
Birdman ft. Lil Wayne - Pop Bottles
Sexyy Red - Pound Town
Kodak Black - Skrilla
The Bellamy Brothers - Let Your Love Flow
Def Leppard - Love Bites
Depeche Mode - People Are People
Captain & Tennille - But I Think It's a Dream
!!! - Off the Grid
Prefab Sprout - Cars and Girls
Cliff Richard - Devil Woman
Chimbala ft. Omega - Se me nota (Agárrame)
Phil Collins - Against All Odds (Take a look at me now)
Elderbrook ft. Bob Moses - Inner Light
GTA 6 se lanza el próximo 19 de noviembre en PlayStation y Xbox de última generación. El vistazo extendido ya está disponible en Netflix y se publicará en YouTube en los siguientes horarios locales:
- España: 03:00 hs del 28 de agosto;
- Reino Unido: 02:00 del 28 de agosto;
- Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 22:00 hs;
- Chile: 21:00 hs;
- Perú, Colombia: 20:00 hs;
- México: 19:00 hs;
- Japón: 10:00 hs del 28 de agosto;
- Australia: 11:00 hs del 28 de agosto;
- Nueva Zelanda: 13:00 hs del 28 de agosto.

articles.title: Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, report claims — could strengthen Nvidia's open-model strategy and shore up position against rivals
articles.text:
Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, report claims — could strengthen Nvidia's open-model strategy and shore up position against rivals
Another major investmnet in AI ecosystem?
Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, according to The Information, citing a person familiar with the deal. If the report is accurate and Nvidia indeed buys Hugging Face, the purchase could strengthen Nvidia's open-model strategy, provide another route to sell AI hardware, and help defend its hardware business as Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other major hyperscalers develop their own accelerators.
Nvidia sells hundreds of billions worth of AI hardware every year. Although the ubiquity of its CUDA software stack and leading performance of its hardware are the primary reasons why Nvidia's AI platforms are sold like hot cakes, another important factor is that many AI models were trained on Nvidia hardware and are optimized to run on it. Therefore, the more models trained on Nvidia hardware, the more products the company is going to sell eventually.
Hugging Face is an AI development platform best known for the Hugging Face Hub, a GitHub-like repository where researchers and developers publish, discover, download, and collaborate on AI models, datasets, and applications. Hugging Face also develops widely used software such as the Transformers library and provides tools and cloud services for training, optimizing, and deploying models on different types of AI hardware.
In addition to hosting models, datasets, and applications, Hugging Face provides software that helps developers optimize and deploy AI models on different CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators, while its Inference Endpoints service lets customers run models on managed infrastructure hosted by AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.
To make things simple, Inference Endpoints allows customers to select the provider, region, hardware type, and instance. What is important here is that the hardware used by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft is not all Nvidia. Hugging Face currently offers, depending on the provider, AWS Inferentia, AMD Instinct, Google TPU, Intel CPUs, and Nvidia accelerators, among other configurations.
OpenAI models, datasets, popular applications, and abilities to optimize and deploy AI models on different hardware make Hugging Face strategically important to Nvidia. On the one hand, the company can make the platform exclusively rely on its hardware, though this may face a backlash from the community, so this is something unlikely to happen in the short term (even assuming Nvidia is indeed set to buy Hugging Face). On the other hand, Nvidia wants open models to remain competitive with proprietary offerings from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI that may eventually get optimized for proprietary non-Nvidia hardware. Nvidia has been building its own Nemotron open models and has committed tens of billions of dollars to the effort. Furthermore, as Hugging Face grows, so is adoption of AI hardware in general and Nvidia hardware in particular.
Hugging Face is growing rapidly, but its revenue remains modest compared with the purchase price, according to The Information. The 10-year-old company recently reached approximately $150 million in annualized revenue, compared with about $100 million several months earlier, which puts Nvidia's price at roughly 80 times forward revenue, something that clearly highlights the strategic nature of the acquisition. Negotiations reportedly began after Hugging Face received acquisition interest elsewhere.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
CEO and co-founder Clem Delangue said in June that paying subscribers doubled during the first half of 2026 and recently said the company was close to profitability. Demand has benefited from improving Chinese open models from Z.ai, Moonshot, and DeepSeek.
If Nvidia proceeds with the takeover, the transaction will be a part of Nvidia's increasingly aggressive investments across the AI ecosystem that spans from hardware to models to software. Last week, Nvidia agreed to pay $6 billion to license development technology from open-model developer Poolside and offered jobs to more than 100 employees. Nvidia also acquired Groq, Enfabrica, Essential AI, Illumex, and Kumo AI, just to name some.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: U.S. 'withdrawing' demands on CanCon discoverability and French labelling: trade minister
articles.text:
The U.S. is walking back its demands for Canada to remove requirements related to Canadian content (CanCon) and bilingual labelling.
U.S.-Canada Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc confirmed the news on X (Twitter), the latest update in a heated trade war between the two countries.
“Canada is pleased that the United States is now reversing its positions regarding discoverability and labelling, and that it confirms that measures aimed at promoting the French language and Canadian culture will not be subject to future trade measures on the part of the United States,” he wrote.
Le Canada se réjouit que les États-Unis reviennent désormais sur leurs positions concernant la découvrabilité et l’étiquetage, et qu’ils confirment que les mesures visant à promouvoir la langue française et la culture canadienne ne feront pas l’objet de futures mesures…
— Dominic LeBlanc (@DLeBlancNB) August 27, 2026
LeBlanc is referring to a series of U.S. demands that Prime Minister Mark Carney said ultimately contributed to trade talks falling through. Specifically, the U.S. had taken issue with Canada requiring foreign streamers like Netflix and Disney+ to promote CanCon on their platform and companies to offer English and French packaging in compliance with Quebec language laws. This came even after Canada axed plans to require U.S. streamers to pay a base requirement into the production of CanCon.
U.S. President Donald Trump, for his part, denied ever making these demands. On his Truth Social platform, he claimed he “would never interfere with Canadians speaking French” and that he loves French Canadians. And because he has the emotional maturity of a toddler, he had to throw in digs at Carney, claiming these demands were “made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec.”
But of course, every accusation is, as they say, a confession, and Trump, who tells tens of thousands of lies, recently held his lowest approval rating at 33 per cent. Carney, by comparison, had a 66 per cent approval rating three weeks ago per Spark, with his highest number (71 per cent) actually coming from Quebec. In other words, that’s quite different from Trump’s claims that the PM has “totally lost” support in the province.
It remains to be seen what else will come out of this awful and unjustified trade war that the U.S. has launched against Canada.
